title: PK Set: SO IT Mains 2026 pattern

sections.name: Professional Knowledge
sections.syllabus: XSS, SHA-256, certificates, MITM, HAVING, BCNF, lossless join, linked list, AVL, A*, PCA, Kubernetes, blockchain, C++/Java/C#, sliding window, TCP window, subnetting, CRC, grep, CPU time, cyclomatic complexity, DPDP Act

qs.q: An attacker posts a comment containing a script on a bank's feedback page. The script is saved in the database and runs in the browser of every customer who opens the page. This is:
qs.e: Stored XSS keeps the malicious script on the server, so it runs for every visitor. Reflected XSS comes back in the immediate response to a crafted link.

qs.q: Which control is the primary defence against cross-site scripting (XSS)?
o: Moving the site from HTTP to HTTPS
Context-aware output encoding of user input, backed by a Content Security Policy
qs.e: XSS is stopped by encoding or escaping untrusted data before it is placed in HTML or JavaScript. CSP limits which scripts can run. Parameterized queries stop SQL injection, not XSS.

qs.q: A SHA-256 digest is written in hexadecimal. How many hexadecimal characters does it contain?
qs.e: SHA-256 gives 256 bits. Each hex character holds 4 bits, so 256 / 4 = 64 characters.

qs.q: Which statement about SHA-256 is correct?
o: SHA-256 can be decrypted if the secret key is known
Changing a single bit of the input changes about half the bits of the digest
Two different inputs can never produce the same digest, even in theory
SHA-256 is a symmetric encryption algorithm
The digest length grows with the size of the input file
qs.e: This is the avalanche effect. SHA-256 is a one-way hash, not encryption, and always gives a 256-bit output. Collisions exist in theory but are infeasible to find.

qs.q: Digital certificates used in TLS/HTTPS follow which standard format?
qs.e: X.509 defines the certificate format: subject, issuer, public key, validity period and the CA's signature.

qs.q: A bank digitally signs a customer's e-statement. The customer verifies the signature using:
qs.e: The signer signs with its own private key. Anyone verifies with the signer's public key, usually taken from its digital certificate.

qs.q: On public Wi-Fi, an attacker sets up a fake access point and silently relays and reads traffic between users and a website. Which attack is this, and which control best defends against it?
o: Man-in-the-middle; TLS with strict certificate validation and HSTS
qs.e: In a MITM attack the attacker sits between two parties. TLS with proper certificate checks, and HSTS to stop downgrade to HTTP, defeats it.

qs.q: Which statement about WHERE and HAVING in SQL is correct?
o: WHERE can use aggregate functions such as SUM() directly
HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY and can use aggregate functions; WHERE filters rows before grouping
HAVING can be used only without GROUP BY
HAVING and WHERE are interchangeable in every query
qs.e: WHERE works on individual rows before grouping. HAVING works on the groups, so conditions like SUM(amount) > 500 go in HAVING.

qs.q: Orders(customer, amount) has rows: (A, 300), (A, 400), (B, 200), (B, 250), (C, 600), (D, 100), (D, 450). How many rows does this query return? SELECT customer FROM Orders GROUP BY customer HAVING SUM(amount) > 500;
qs.e: Totals: A = 700, B = 450, C = 600, D = 550. Three customers (A, C, D) have totals above 500.

qs.q: What is the logical order in which SQL processes these clauses?
o: FROM, WHERE, HAVING, GROUP BY, SELECT, ORDER BY
SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
SELECT, WHERE, FROM, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, HAVING
FROM, GROUP BY, WHERE, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY
FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY
qs.e: Rows are fetched (FROM), filtered (WHERE), grouped, filtered as groups (HAVING), then projected (SELECT) and sorted last.

qs.q: R(S, C, T) stores student, course and teacher, with functional dependencies SC → T and T → C. Which statement is correct?
o: R is in 3NF but not in BCNF
R has only one candidate key, SC
R is in 2NF but not in 3NF
qs.e: Candidate keys are SC and ST. In T → C, T is not a super key, so BCNF fails. C is a prime attribute, so 3NF holds.

qs.q: The same R(S, C, T) with SC → T and T → C is decomposed into R1(T, C) and R2(S, T). This decomposition is:
o: Lossy, but all dependencies are preserved
Lossless only if T is the primary key of R2
Lossless, but SC → T is not preserved
qs.e: The common attribute T determines all of R1 (T → C), so the join is lossless. SC → T cannot be checked in either table alone, so it is lost. This is the classic BCNF trade-off.

qs.q: R(A, B, C, D) has functional dependencies A → BC and C → D. Which decomposition is lossless?
qs.e: For ABC and CD the common attribute is C, and C → D, so C is a key of R2: lossless. The other pairs share no attribute, or share one that is not a key of either part.

qs.q: A decomposition of R into R1 and R2 is lossless if and only if:
o: R1 and R2 have no common attribute
R1 ∪ R2 has fewer attributes than R
(R1 ∩ R2) → R1 or (R1 ∩ R2) → R2 holds
Both R1 and R2 are in BCNF
qs.e: The common attributes must be a super key of at least one of the two relations. Dependency preservation is a separate property.

qs.q: In a singly linked list with only a head pointer, which operation takes O(n) time?
o: Inserting a node at the beginning
Reading the data of the first node
Checking whether the list is empty
qs.e: To delete the last node you must walk to the second-last node, which takes n steps. The other operations work at the head in O(1).

qs.q: Which technique detects a cycle in a linked list using O(1) extra space?
o: Storing every visited node in a hash set
Floyd's tortoise and hare (slow and fast pointers)
qs.e: One pointer moves one step, the other two steps. If there is a cycle they meet. A hash set also works but needs O(n) space.

qs.q: What is the minimum number of nodes in an AVL tree of height 5? (A single-node tree has height 0.)
Keys 30, 20, 10 are inserted in this order into an empty AVL tree. Which rebalancing is done and what is the final root?
qs.e: 10 goes to the left of 20, which is left of 30: the LL case. One right rotation at 30 makes 20 the root, with 10 and 30 as children.

qs.q: Keys 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 25 are inserted in this order into an empty AVL tree. What is the root of the final tree?
qs.e: After 10 to 50 the tree is 20 (10, 40 (30, 50)). Inserting 25 unbalances 20 in the right-left case, so a double rotation makes 30 the root: 30 (20 (10, 25), 40 (50)).

qs.q: In A* search the open list holds: P (g = 4, h = 7), Q (g = 6, h = 3), R (g = 2, h = 10), S (g = 5, h = 5). Which node is expanded next?
qs.e: A* expands the lowest f = g + h. P = 11, Q = 9, R = 12, S = 10, so Q comes next.

qs.q: A* search is guaranteed to find an optimal path (in tree search) when its heuristic h(n) is:
o: Always larger than the true cost
Admissible: it never overestimates the true cost to the goal
qs.e: An admissible heuristic never overestimates. With h(n) = 0, A* becomes uniform-cost search: still optimal, but slower.

qs.q: In Principal Component Analysis (PCA), the principal components are:
o: Eigenvectors of the data's covariance matrix, ordered by the variance they explain
The labels used to train the model
The original features ranked by importance
qs.e: PCA finds new orthogonal axes along the directions of greatest variance. The eigenvalues give the variance captured by each axis.

qs.q: The eigenvalues of a dataset's covariance matrix are 5, 3, 1.5 and 0.5. What percentage of the total variance do the first two principal components explain?
Why are features usually standardized before applying PCA?
o: Standardization removes the need to compute a covariance matrix
It guarantees that every component explains equal variance
It converts PCA into a supervised method
Features with larger numeric ranges would otherwise dominate the variance
PCA works only on categorical data
qs.e: PCA follows variance. A feature measured in rupees would overshadow one measured as a ratio unless both are scaled.

qs.q: What is the smallest deployable unit that Kubernetes creates and manages?
qs.e: A Pod wraps one or more containers that share network and storage. Kubernetes schedules Pods, not bare containers.

qs.q: Which Kubernetes object gives a stable IP address and DNS name to a changing set of Pods?
qs.e: Pods come and go with new IPs. A Service selects them by label and gives clients one stable endpoint. A Deployment manages replicas and rolling updates.

qs.q: Why does changing a transaction in an old block of a blockchain get detected immediately?
o: Old blocks are deleted after a fixed time
The block is encrypted with the miner's private key
Blocks are stored only on one central server
The transaction amounts must add up to zero
Each block stores the hash of the previous block, so every later hash link breaks
qs.e: Editing a block changes its hash, which no longer matches the previous-hash field in the next block. The whole chain after it becomes invalid.

qs.q: What is the purpose of a Merkle tree (Merkle root) in a block?
o: To encrypt transactions so only miners can read them
To store the private keys of users
To compress the blockchain to a single block
To prove a transaction is included in a block without downloading every transaction
qs.e: Transaction hashes are paired and hashed up to one root. A light client checks inclusion with only log(n) hashes.

qs.q: In C++, class A has a properly defined copy constructor. Which of these statements does NOT call it?
o: Initializing a new A object from an existing one
Passing an object of A to a function by value
qs.e: A b; b = a; first default-constructs b, then calls the copy assignment operator. The other cases create a new object from an existing one, which calls the copy constructor.

qs.q: In C++, a class defines only a parameterized constructor A(int x). What happens with the statement A obj; ?
o: The compiler calls the copy constructor
Compilation error, because no default constructor is generated
obj is created with a garbage value of x
It compiles but crashes at run time
qs.e: Once you declare any constructor, the compiler does not generate a default constructor. You must write A() yourself or give x a default value.

qs.q: In C++, class B publicly inherits class A. An object of B is created and then destroyed. What is the order of calls?
o: Only B's constructor and destructor run
B constructor, A constructor, A destructor, B destructor
B constructor, A constructor, B destructor, A destructor
A constructor, B constructor, A destructor, B destructor
A constructor, B constructor, B destructor, A destructor
qs.e: The base part is built first and destroyed last. Destructors run in reverse order of construction.

qs.q: Which statement about the Java final keyword is correct?
o: A final class can be extended by an abstract class
A final method cannot be overloaded
A final method can be overloaded but cannot be overridden
A method can be declared both final and abstract
A final instance variable must be initialized at the point of declaration only
qs.e: Overloading creates a new method with a different signature, which is allowed. A blank final field may also be set in every constructor. final and abstract contradict each other.

qs.q: In Java: final List<String> list = new ArrayList<>(); list.add("x"); list = new ArrayList<>(); What happens?
o: Compilation error only at the reassignment line; adding elements is allowed
The list becomes immutable after the first add
Both lines compile and run without error
qs.e: final fixes the reference, not the object. You can change the list's contents but cannot point list to a new object.

qs.q: In C#, what does the await keyword do inside an async method?
o: It starts a new operating system thread for the method
It cancels the task if it takes too long
It suspends the method until the awaited task completes, without blocking the calling thread
It converts a synchronous method into a parallel loop
It blocks the current thread until the task finishes
qs.e: At await, control returns to the caller and the thread is freed. The method resumes when the task completes, which is how UIs and servers stay responsive.

qs.q: In C#, which return type is recommended for an async method that returns no value and is not an event handler?
qs.e: async void is meant only for event handlers, because callers cannot await it or catch its exceptions. Task<void> does not exist.

qs.q: A Selective Repeat protocol uses 3-bit sequence numbers. What is the maximum sender window size?
qs.e: For Selective Repeat the window can be at most 2^(n−1) = 2^2 = 4. Go-Back-N allows 2^n − 1 = 7.

qs.q: A Go-Back-N sender with window size 4 sends frames 0, 1, 2 and 3. Frame 1 is lost; the others arrive. How many frames does the sender retransmit after frame 1 times out?
qs.e: The receiver discards 2 and 3 because 1 is missing, so the sender resends 1, 2 and 3. Selective Repeat would resend only frame 1.

qs.q: A TCP connection uses a window of 65,535 bytes (no window scaling) on a path with a round-trip time of 20 ms. What is the maximum throughput?
qs.e: Throughput is at most window / RTT = 65,535 × 8 bits / 0.020 s = 26.2 Mbps, however fast the link is.

qs.q: What minimum TCP window size is needed to fully use a 100 Mbps link with a round-trip time of 40 ms?
qs.e: Bandwidth-delay product = 100 × 10^6 × 0.040 / 8 = 500,000 bytes. This is above 65,535, so TCP window scaling is needed.

qs.q: What is the broadcast address of the subnet that contains host 192.168.10.77/27?
qs.e: A /27 block has 32 addresses: 64 to 95. 77 falls in it, so the network is .64 and the broadcast is .95, with 30 usable hosts.

qs.q: A bank splits 172.16.0.0/16 into subnets that each need at least 50 hosts. Which mask gives the largest number of such subnets?
qs.e: /26 (255.255.255.192) gives 62 usable hosts, enough for 50, and the most subnets (1,024). /27 gives only 30 hosts.

qs.q: The message 1101011011 is sent using CRC with generator 10011 (x^4 + x + 1). Which 4-bit CRC is appended?
qs.e: Append four 0s and divide 11010110110000 by 10011 using XOR. The remainder 1110 is appended, so the frame sent is 11010110111110.

qs.q: Which command prints the number of lines in app.log that do NOT contain the word ERROR?
qs.e: -v inverts the match and -c counts the lines. -n shows line numbers, -l lists file names, -w matches whole words.

qs.q: Which command lists only the names of files under /var/log, searched recursively, that contain the text timeout?
qs.e: -r searches subdirectories and -l prints just the matching file names. -c prints counts per file, -o prints only the matched text.

qs.q: Which Linux command records everything shown in a terminal session into a file, which can later be played back with scriptreplay?
qs.e: script saves the session (by default to a file named typescript). With timing data, scriptreplay plays it back. history keeps only typed commands, not output.

qs.q: Processor P1 runs at 3 GHz with an average CPI of 1.5. Processor P2 runs at 2.5 GHz with an average CPI of 1.0. Both run the same program. Which is faster, and by how much?
qs.e: Time per instruction = CPI / clock. P1: 1.5 / 3 GHz = 0.5 ns. P2: 1.0 / 2.5 GHz = 0.4 ns. 0.5 / 0.4 = 1.25.

qs.q: A function's control flow graph has 14 edges and 11 nodes, with one connected component. What is its cyclomatic complexity?
qs.e: V(G) = E − N + 2P = 14 − 11 + 2 × 1 = 5. This is also the number of independent paths to test.

qs.q: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the person or entity that decides the purpose and means of processing personal data is called the:
qs.e: The Data Fiduciary decides why and how data is processed, for example a bank. The Data Principal is the individual the data belongs to.

qs.q: What is the maximum penalty under the DPDP Act, 2023 for failing to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach?
qs.e: ₹250 crore is the highest penalty. Failing to report a breach, or violations about children's data, can cost up to ₹200 crore. Other violations up to ₹50 crore. The 4% turnover rule belongs to Europe's GDPR.

qs.q: Under the DPDP framework, what does a Data Fiduciary need before processing the personal data of a child?
o: Verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian
Approval of the Data Protection Board for each case
No consent, if the data is stored in India
qs.e: Children's data needs verifiable consent from a parent or lawful guardian. The Rules allow exceptions for things like healthcare, education and real-time safety.
